newsitem.title: USA: Merck parasite drug approved by FDA.
newsitem.headline: Merck parasite drug approved by FDA.

text.p: An anti-parasite drug widely used in developing countries received federal Food and Drug Administration approval Monday for use in the United States.
The drug invermectin, marketed under the brand name Stromectol by Merck and Co. Inc., was previously approved for veterinary use only in the United States.

It is useful against two parasites. One, strongyloidiasis, is rare in the United States and usually affects only people who have become infected overseas. The other, onchocerciasis, causes the disease known as river blindness in Africa and Latin America.
More than 5.2 million people have received invermectin worldwide in a campaign to wipe out river blindness.
